description:
¡Hola! Somos SAFER de San Pedro Sula. Nos apasiona la tecnología, el análisis de datos y la agricultura. Participamos en el reto "Field Shift" para transformar las granjas usando datos de la NASA.

Únete a nosotros si quieres crear un impacto real y proteger el futuro del campo. Buscamos mentes creativas: desarrolladores, analistas de datos, diseñadores y expertos en agronomía.

¡Hagamos equipo y llevemos la tecnología espacial directamente a la agricultura!
summary:
We developed SAFER, an interactive geospatial decision-support web application that helps farmers design climate-resilient 3-cycle crop rotation plans. 

Using a KML/GeoJSON upload or an interactive satellite map, SAFER combines live NASA Earth observations—including NASA POWER climate series, NASA GIBS NDVI and precipitation layers, NASA CMR STAC Sentinel-2 imagery, and NASA EONET hazard events—with ISRIC SoilGrids local soil data, agronomic crop traits, and five farmer-weighted priorities. 

Its Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) engine enforces botanical-family rotation rules to break pest cycles, builds a 3D Farm Digital Twin, and runs "What-If" simulations for severe drought (-25% rainfall) and heat waves (+2.0°C). By turning complex satellite datasets into clear, field-ready planting strategies without requiring GIS expertise, SAFER empowers farmers to conserve water, restore soil organic matter, and stabilize yields under climate stress.
details:
Live Application: https://safer-sepia.vercel.app/

Source Code (GitHub): https://github.com/504-Sistemas/SAFER

1. What It Does & How It Works

SAFER is a full-stack geospatial decision-support web application that helps farmers design climate-resilient 3-cycle annual crop rotation plans. Users can upload a .kml or GeoJSON field boundary, load real-world sample farms (Finca1.kml–finca5.kml), or draw a parcel directly on an interactive satellite map. SAFER automatically computes the centroid, bounding box, and geodesic area in hectares, then runs a multi-source analysis:

- Agroclimatic & Satellite Diagnosis: Fetches historical climatology and daily rainfall/temperature series from NASA POWER, searches Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLSS30.v2.0) scenes via NASA CMR STAC, overlays live NASA GIBS WMTS raster layers (MODIS Terra 8-Day NDVI and GPM IMERG Precipitation Rate), and checks nearby natural hazards via NASA EONET.

- Local Soil & Farmer Priorities: Queries ISRIC SoilGrids v2.0 (0–5 cm texture, pH, organic carbon) with an optional manual override for local lab tests, and lets farmers weight five priorities (0–100%): Water Conservation, Soil Health & Organic Matter, Natural Pest Control, Economic Stability, and Climate Resilience.

- MCDA Rotation Engine & What-If Simulator: Evaluates 3-cycle sequences across a 9-crop agronomic catalog, outputting the Top 3 rotations with cycle-by-cycle justifications, fungal/insect pest risk assessments, a 3D Farm Digital Twin, and "What-If" stress simulations comparing the farmer's current monoculture against Rotation #1 under Normal Climate, Severe Drought (-25% rainfall), and Heat Wave (+2.0°C).

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

Farmers—especially smallholders in climate-vulnerable regions like Central America—face irregular rainfall, droughts, heat stress, and soil degradation from repeated monoculture, yet lack GIS expertise to interpret satellite data. SAFER translates orbital observations into actionable planting schedules in seconds, helping farmers conserve water, rebuild soil organic matter with nitrogen-fixing legumes and cover crops, break pest cycles naturally, and stabilize yields under extreme weather.

3. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

- Backend: C# / .NET 10 (ASP.NET Core Web API), IMemoryCache (2–12 hour TTL caching and regional fallbacks), custom KML/GeoJSON parser, 6x6 terrain elevation grid service, MCDA rotation engine, and unit tests (Safer.Tests).

- Frontend: TypeScript 5.7, Angular 19.2, RxJS, SCSS, Leaflet 1.9 (interactive map + NASA GIBS WMTS overlays), and Three.js 0.187 (3D Farm Digital Twin).

- Infrastructure & Deployment: Docker (multi-stage .NET 10 container), Vercel (web hosting), Git/GitHub, and standard developer workstations.

4. How It Is Creative

Instead of showing static climate charts or requiring complex GIS software, SAFER unifies live NASA satellite layers, a 3D terrain digital twin of the user's actual field, customizable farmer priority sliders, and a forward-looking "What-If" drought/heat-wave simulator into a single, intuitive workflow.

5. Factors Considered

Our team considered real-world field constraints: API latency and offline resilience (addressed with in-memory caching and regional fallbacks), differences between global soil estimates and local lab tests (addressed with manual soil overrides), agronomic guardrails (prohibiting consecutive crops of the same botanical family, checking pH/temperature/water thresholds), and high-contrast, accessible UI design for rural technicians and farmers.
